Russia is one of the key and largest donors to the WFP, and supports its work in many countries. Since 2003, the Russian authorities have allocated more than 430 million US dollars worldwide to support WFP humanitarian operations and development projects.
Read the full text of the interview on the website ria.ru at 9.00 Moscow time.

a4235.t:
Après les trois autres associations de la société civile appartenant toutes au groupe appelé cluster, l’association IFTIN a remis, à son tour, des réservoirs d’eau potable à une centaine de ménages vulnérables issus de quatre quartiers différents de la ville d’Ali-Sabieh.
Pour rappel l’association avait obtenu un financement pour une lutte efficace contre l’inaccessible à l’eau potable. La subvention de financement accordée par l’USAID, l’agence de la coopération internationale des Etats-Unis d’Amérique contribuera à l’objectif global. Il s’agit du Projet d’Appui à l’Engagement de la Société Civile dans le Processus de Développement Local (CEAA), qui vise à améliorer l’accès à l’eau et à fournir les moyens de conservation appropriés.
Auparavant, les membres de l’association IFTIN ont formé cent mères de famille bénéficiaires de bombonnes de 320 litres de capacités. Elle a organisé plusieurs formations et activités de sensibilisation sur l’hygiène, la gravité de la violence basée sur le genre, discutant de la prévention et des ressources disponibles pour les victimes, ainsi qu’à l’utilisation à bon escient et à l’entretien des bonbonnes ou de leur réservoir d’eau potable. Un projet exécuté par les associations : AJCD, IFTIN, APTDD et APAM sous la thématique “Harmoniser l’équilibre entre le genre et l’eau”. Une donation de réservoir d’eau potable qui vise à répondre aux besoins des femmes et des filles vulnérables en matière d’accès à l’eau potable. Ces organisations appartenant au milieu associatif régional ont tous mis en œuvre un projet similaire qui s’inscrit dans le cadre de la lutte contre la soif.
A l’instar de ces groupements, l’association IFTIN fait partie du cluster d’Ali-Sabieh qui a été formé dans le cadre du Projet d’Appui à l’Engagement de la Société Civile Dans le Processus du Développement Local, mis en œuvre par The Kaizen Company et financé par USAID. Grâce à ce projet novateur et avec le soutien constant de The Kaizen Company et avec l’appui financier de l’USAID, l’association a bénéficié d’un renforcement de capacité avec des formations approfondies dans divers domaines tels que la gestion financière, la mobilisation de ressource, stratégie de communication, la planification stratégique, le suivi et l’évaluation, renforçant ainsi leur capacité à contribuer de manière significative au développement local. Cette activité s’inscrit dans le cadre du projet d’Appui à l’engagement de la société civile, financé par l’USAID et mis en œuvre par The Kaizen Company. Cet événement, tenu au siège de l’association, a vu la participation active des responsables du ministère de la Femme et de la Famille, du Conseil régional et des autres organisations de la société civile, ainsi qu’une délégation de The Kaizen Company, le comité exécutif de l’association, dirigé par Madame la Présidente de l’association, Chef de Projet les femmes bénéficiaires du programme.
La présidente de l’association IFTIN, Moumina Okieh a qualifié cette initiative de réussite. Les femmes participantes des différentes formations ont assimilé des connaissances précieuses et une motivation renouvelée, a-t-elle souligné.
Elle a fini son intervention que l’Association IFTIN ALI-SABIEH continue de jouer un rôle clé dans le développement communautaire, prouvant une fois de plus son dévouement et son efficacité.
Quant au secrétaire général du conseil régional, Aden Abdillahi Ali a félicité les membres de l’association pour leur engagement dans des actions à caractère social. L’association joue un rôle non négligeable dans la gestion des détritus populaire dans le quartier Barwako.
A l’issue de la distribution des réservoirs d’eau potable, les bénéficiaires ont remercié les membres de l’association IFTIN. Une remise de bombonne qui renforcera notre capacité de stockage du liquide précieux et qui intervient en pleine saison chaude.
Ali Ladieh
a4235.en:
After the three other civil society associations all belonging to the group known as the cluster, the IFTIN association has in its turn handed over drinking-water tanks to some hundred vulnerable households from four different neighbourhoods of the town of Ali-Sabieh.

As a reminder, the association had obtained funding for an effective fight against the inaccessibility of drinking water. The funding grant awarded by USAID, the international cooperation agency of the United States of America, will contribute to the overall objective. This is the Project of Support to the Engagement of Civil Society in the Local Development Process (CEAA), which aims to improve access to water and to provide appropriate means of conservation.

Beforehand, the members of the IFTIN association had trained one hundred mothers of families who are beneficiaries of 320-litre tanks. It organised several training sessions and awareness activities on hygiene, on the gravity of gender-based violence – discussing prevention and the resources available for victims – as well as on the proper use and maintenance of the containers or their drinking-water tanks. A project executed by the associations AJCD, IFTIN, APTDD and APAM under the theme "Harmonising the balance between gender and water". A donation of drinking-water tanks that aims to respond to the needs of vulnerable women and girls with regard to access to drinking water. These organisations belonging to the regional associative milieu have all implemented a similar project which falls within the framework of the fight against thirst.

Like these groupings, the IFTIN association is part of the Ali-Sabieh cluster, which was formed within the framework of the Project of Support to the Engagement of Civil Society in the Local Development Process, implemented by The Kaizen Company and financed by USAID. Thanks to this innovative project, and with the constant support of The Kaizen Company and the financial backing of USAID, the association benefited from capacity building with in-depth training in various fields such as financial management, resource mobilisation, communication strategy, strategic planning, and monitoring and evaluation, thereby strengthening their capacity to contribute significantly to local development. This activity falls within the framework of the Project of Support to the Engagement of Civil Society, financed by USAID and implemented by The Kaizen Company. This event, held at the headquarters of the association, saw the active participation of officials of the Ministry of Women and Family, of the Regional Council and of the other civil society organisations, as well as a delegation from The Kaizen Company, the executive committee of the association, headed by the Madam President of the association, the Project Manager, and the women beneficiaries of the programme.

The president of the IFTIN association, Moumina Okieh, described this initiative as a success. The women who participated in the various training sessions assimilated valuable knowledge and renewed motivation, she stressed.

She ended her intervention by saying that the IFTIN ALI-SABIEH Association continues to play a key role in community development, proving once again its dedication and its effectiveness.

As for the secretary general of the regional council, Aden Abdillahi Ali, he congratulated the members of the association for their commitment to actions of a social character. The association plays a not inconsiderable role in the management of the refuse that is widespread in the Barwako neighbourhood.

At the end of the distribution of the drinking-water tanks, the beneficiaries thanked the members of the IFTIN association. A handover of containers that will strengthen our storage capacity for the precious liquid and that comes in the middle of the hot season.

Ali Ladieh

a4534.t:
Muktasari:
- USAID ilizindua mradi wa uhifadhi wenye thamani ya Dola milioni 30.5 za Marekani (zaidi ya Sh75 bilioni) kwa kipindi cha miaka mitano, kuanzia mwaka 2022 hadi 2026, kabla ya kusitishwa mwanzoni mwa mwaka huu.
Arusha. Ubalozi wa Marekani nchini umethibitisha kuwa miradi ya maendeleo iliyokuwa ikitekelezwa kupitia Shirika la Maendeleo ya Kimataifa la Marekani (USAID) itarejeshwa, licha ya shirika hilo kufungwa mapema mwaka huu.
Kauli hiyo imetolewa leo Jumapili, Septemba 14, 2025, na Balozi wa muda wa Marekani nchini, Andrew Lentz, alipozungumza na waandishi wa habari jijini Arusha baada ya kumaliza ziara yake katika mikoa ya kanda ya kaskazini.
Balozi Lentz amesema kufungwa kwa USAID hakumaanishi mwisho wa miradi ya maendeleo, bali kutakuwepo na mfumo mpya wa utekelezaji ili kuhakikisha miradi hiyo inaendelea.
Amebainisha kuwa Marekani itashirikiana na mashirika mbalimbali na jamii za wenyeji kuchukua jukumu la kusimamia baadhi ya miradi iliyokuwa chini ya USAID.
“Tutahakikisha miradi inafanyika tena kwa kushirikiana na wadau wa ndani na wa kimataifa. Lengo letu ni kuendeleza jitihada za uhifadhi na maendeleo ya kijamii,” amesema.
Miongoni mwa miradi iliyopewa kipaumbele ni urejeshaji wa korido za wanyamapori, ambazo ni muhimu kwa mtiririko wa ikolojia. Tanzania ina jumla ya korido 61 za wanyamapori, nyingi zikiwa zimeharibika au kuzibwa kutokana na shughuli za kibinadamu.
Kupitia mradi wa Tuhifadhi Maliasili uliokuwa ukifadhiliwa na USAID, juhudi za kuzifungua korido hizo zilianza kwa ushirikiano na Wizara ya Maliasili na Utalii pamoja na wadau wengine wa uhifadhi.
Awali, USAID ilizindua mradi wa uhifadhi wenye thamani ya Dola milioni 30.5 za Marekani (zaidi ya Sh75 bilioni) mwaka 2022, uliopangwa kutekelezwa kwa miaka mitano hadi mwaka 2026, kwa lengo la kukabiliana na changamoto zinazotishia uhamaji wa wanyamapori na kuhifadhi bayoanuai.
Hata hivyo, mradi huo pamoja na mingine mingi ulisitishwa mapema mwaka huu chini ya utawala wa Rais Donald Trump.
Mbali na sekta ya uhifadhi, USAID iliwahi kutoa zaidi ya Dola milioni 400 kusaidia kuimarisha biashara, kukuza ajira na kuharakisha maendeleo ya Tanzania.
Vilevile, Shirika la Fedha la Maendeleo la Marekani (DFC) lilitangaza mkopo wa zaidi ya Dola milioni 300 kwa Benki ya CRDB mwaka 2024, uliokusudiwa kusaidia zaidi ya biashara ndogo 4,500.
Aidha, DFC na USAID kwa pamoja walitoa dhamana ya mikopo ya ziada yenye thamani ya Dola milioni 52 kwa Benki za Amana na CRDB, fedha ambazo zilielekezwa katika sekta za elimu, uchumi usio rasmi, kilimo, biashara za wanawake na vijana pamoja na afya.
Miongoni mwa wadau wa uhifadhi, shirika la World Wildlife Fund (WWF) limeeleza matumaini kuwa hatua ya kurejesha miradi hiyo inaweza kwenda sambamba na urejeo wa ufadhili kupitia Shirika la Changamoto ya Milenia la Marekani (MCC).
a4534.en:
Summary:
- USAID launched a conservation project worth 30.5 million US dollars (more than 75 billion shillings) for a five-year period, from 2022 to 2026, before it was halted earlier this year.

Arusha. The United States Embassy in the country has confirmed that development projects that were being implemented through the United States Agency for International Development (USAID) will be restored, despite the agency having been closed earlier this year.

That statement was made today, Sunday, September 14, 2025, by the acting US Ambassador to the country, Andrew Lentz, when he spoke to journalists in the city of Arusha after completing his tour of the northern zone regions.

Ambassador Lentz said that the closure of USAID does not mean the end of development projects, but rather that there will be a new implementation framework to ensure those projects continue.

He explained that the United States will collaborate with various organisations and local communities to take on the responsibility of managing some of the projects that were under USAID.

"We will ensure the projects are carried out again in collaboration with local and international stakeholders. Our goal is to advance conservation efforts and social development," he said.

Among the projects given priority is the restoration of wildlife corridors, which are important for ecological flow. Tanzania has a total of 61 wildlife corridors, many of which have been degraded or blocked as a result of human activities.

Through the Tuhifadhi Maliasili project, which was funded by USAID, efforts to reopen those corridors began in collaboration with the Ministry of Natural Resources and Tourism together with other conservation stakeholders.

Earlier, USAID launched a conservation project worth 30.5 million US dollars (more than 75 billion shillings) in 2022, planned to be implemented over five years until 2026, with the aim of confronting the challenges that threaten wildlife migration and of conserving biodiversity.

However, that project, along with many others, was halted earlier this year under the administration of President Donald Trump.

Besides the conservation sector, USAID had previously provided more than 400 million dollars to help strengthen business, grow employment and accelerate Tanzania's development.

Likewise, the US Development Finance Corporation (DFC) announced a loan of more than 300 million dollars to CRDB Bank in 2024, intended to support more than 4,500 small businesses.

In addition, the DFC and USAID jointly provided additional loan guarantees worth 52 million dollars to Amana and CRDB banks, funds which were directed towards the sectors of education, the informal economy, agriculture, women's and youth businesses, as well as health.

Among conservation stakeholders, the World Wildlife Fund (WWF) has expressed hope that the move to restore those projects could go hand in hand with the return of funding through the United States Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC).

a4577.t:
Muktasari:
- Mchakato wa rufaa ni sehemu muhimu ya mfumo wa kidemokrasia, unaotoa nafasi kwa wale wanaoamini kuwa walikosewa kutafuta haki.
Dar es Salaam. Utulivu, subira na utayari wa kukubaliana na hatima ni mambo matatu muhimu yanayopaswa kuwa mwongozo kwa wagombea wa nafasi za uongozi, wakati huu wa kusubiri matokeo ya rufaa.
Katika kipindi hiki, moyo unapaswa kuwa thabiti na akili iendelee kuwa tulivu, kwani hatima yao iko mikononi mwa taasisi na mamlaka zinazohusika na kutoa uamuzi wa mwisho.
Kuthamini mchakato wa kisheria
Mchakato wa rufaa ni sehemu muhimu ya mfumo wa kidemokrasia, unaotoa nafasi kwa wale wanaoamini kuwa walikosewa kutafuta haki.
Kwa msingi huo, wagombea wanapaswa kuelewa na kuthamini kwamba mchakato huo unalenga kuweka uwazi na haki katika mchakato mzima wa uchaguzi.
Kuwa na subira
Katika dunia ya sasa, subira imekuwa ni nadra, kila mtu hutaka majibu ya haraka.
Hata hivyo, wakati wa mchakato wa rufaa, wagombea wanapaswa kukumbuka kuwa majibu sahihi yanahitaji muda.
Kulingana na takwimu za Tume Huru ya Taifa ya Uchaguzi (INEC), rufaa nyingi huamuliwa ndani ya kipindi cha chini ya wiki moja, lakini hali hii hutegemea pia uzito wa hoja za kila rufaa.
Kuweka subira kunawasaidia wagombea kuepuka majuto na vurugu, huku wakiheshimu muda wa kila hatua ya mchakato.
Kujiandaa kwa matokeo yoyote
Hali ya kutojua kilichopo mbele inaweza kuwa na changamoto kisaikolojia kwa wagombea wengi.
Uchunguzi wa Shirika la Tafiti za Kisiasa Tanzania mwaka 2021, ulionyesha asilimia 40 ya wagombea waliokataliwa na tume za uchaguzi waliingia kwenye unyong’onyevu baada ya rufaa zao kushindwa.
Ni muhimu, basi, kwa wagombea kuwa na mtazamo wa kukubali matokeo yoyote ili kuweza kuendelea na maisha yao, wakifahamu kuwa nafasi ya uongozi siyo mwisho wa dunia.
Kuweka mikakati ya baadaye
Kusubiri huku kunaweza kutumiwa kwa hekima kwa ajili ya kutafakari mikakati ya muda mrefu.
Iwapo hautafanikiwa kupitia rufaa, wagombea wanapaswa kujiuliza, nini kinachofuata, kuwa na mpango wa baadaye ni sehemu ya udhibiti wa maisha yao na husaidia kupunguza athari za kisaikolojia.
Hii imeonekana kwa wagombea wengi walioacha michakato ya siasa na kujikita kwenye shughuli nyingine za kijamii, hatua ambayo imesaidia kuchangia maendeleo katika jamii.
Kuwa kielelezo kwa wafuasi wako
Katika kipindi hiki kigumu, wafuasi wa mgombea hujawa na hamasa na matarajio makubwa.
Takwimu za mwaka 2019 za Jeshi la Polisi zinaonyesha asilimia 60 ya vurugu zilizoripotiwa wakati wa uchaguzi wa serikali za mitaa, zilisababishwa na wafuasi waliokuwa hawajaridhishwa na matokeo ya rufaa za wagombea wao.
Wagombea wana jukumu la kuwa mfano mzuri kwa wafuasi wao kwa kuwaelekeza kuheshimu sheria na kusubiri kwa utulivu, hali ambayo pia inaweza kusaidia kudumisha amani na utulivu katika jamii.
Kuzingatia maadili na ustaarabu katika kauli na matendo
Wakati wa kusubiri, inashauriwa kwa wagombea kuepuka kauli zinazosababisha mgawanyiko na chuki katika jamii.
Mgombea anapaswa kuwa na lugha ya kistaarabu, akiwakilisha heshima na uaminifu kwa wote.
Utafiti wa Chuo Kikuu cha Dar es Salaam (UDSM) mwaka 2021, umebaini wagombea wanaojenga picha chanya kwa jamii kupitia kauli na matendo yao wana nafasi kubwa ya kupata uungwaji mkono wa kudumu hata baada ya uchaguzi.
Kuweka akili katika shughuli nyingine za maendeleo
Badala ya kukaa na kusubiri bila kufanya chochote, wagombea wanaweza kujihusisha na shughuli mbalimbali za kijamii.
Tafiti zinaonyesha asilimia 45 ya wagombea wanaojihusisha na shughuli za kujitolea katika jamii, waliongeza uungwaji mkono wao katika chaguzi za baadaye kwa mujibu wa Shirika la Kimataifa la Misaada na Maendeleo la USAID.
Hii inadhihirisha kuwa kujishughulisha katika mambo mengine ya kijamii si tu kunawasaidia kusahau changamoto za uchaguzi, bali pia kunawapa nafasi ya kuendelea kuwa karibu na jamii yao.
Kutafuta ushauri wa kitaalamu
Wakati mwingine, msongo wa mawazo unaotokana na hali ya kutokuwa na uhakika unaweza kumlemea mgombea.
Ushauri wa kitaalamu wa kisaikolojia unaweza kumsaidia mgombea kuwa na mtazamo bora wakati wa kusubiri.
Shirika la Afya Duniani (WHO) linaonyesha kuwa asilimia 15 ya watu wanaoshiriki kwenye siasa, huwa na viwango vya juu vya msongo wa mawazo, hasa wakati wa kusubiri matokeo muhimu kama hayo.
Huduma hizi za kitaalamu zinaweza kumsaidia mgombea kupata nguvu ya kuendelea na safari ya kisiasa au kuchukua mwelekeo mwingine katika maisha yake.
Kujifunza kutokana na mchakato
Kila hatua katika siasa ina somo, na kipindi cha kusubiri rufaa ni fursa nzuri ya kujifunza.
Wagombea wanaweza kuchambua nguvu na udhaifu wao, kutathmini ni wapi walikosea na wapi walifanya vizuri.
Tafiti kutoka Kituo cha Demokrasia na Maendeleo mwaka 2022, zinaonyesha asilimia 70 ya wagombea waliopitia rufaa walirudi na mipango thabiti na mikakati bora zaidi ya kushiriki uchaguzi wa baadaye.
Hii inamaanisha kuwa kutumia muda huu kwa kujifunza kunaweza kuwa njia bora ya kujitayarisha kwa changamoto zijazo.
Kusubiri matokeo ya rufaa si jambo jepesi, lakini ni sehemu muhimu ya safari ya kisiasa.
Ni wakati unaohitaji uvumilivu, hekima na utayari wa kukubaliana na hatima yoyote.
Kwa kuelewa na kuheshimu mchakato wa rufaa, kuthamini subira, kuwa mfano kwa wafuasi wao, na kujiandaa kwa hatua zijazo, wagombea wanaweza kubaki imara na kuendelea kuwa na matumaini kwa ajili ya jamii wanayotaka kuongoza.
Mfumo wa kidemokrasia unawawezesha wananchi kutafuta haki, kadhalika unahitaji wajibu wa kuwa na nidhamu na uaminifu.
Kuimarisha uhusiano na wadau muhimu
Katika siasa, uhusiano na mtandao wa wadau ni nyenzo muhimu ambayo inaweza kumsaidia mgombea kujiimarisha kisiasa hata katika mazingira yenye changamoto.
Wakati wa kusubiri matokeo ya rufaa, ni fursa mwafaka kwa wagombea kujenga na kudumisha uhusiano na viongozi wa kisiasa, wanaharakati, na wanajamii wenye ushawishi mkubwa.
Utafiti uliofanywa na Taasisi ya Masuala ya Siasa na Demokrasia (TPDI) mwaka 2021, umebaini asilimia 35 ya wagombea walioshirikiana na wadau muhimu walipata nafasi nzuri ya kupata uungwaji mkono kwa kipindi kirefu, licha ya changamoto walizokutana nazo wakati wa uchaguzi.
Katika kipindi hiki cha kusubiri, wagombea wanapaswa kutumia muda wao kwa busara kwa kushiriki katika shughuli za kijamii zinazowajenga wao na kuwajumuisha katika mitandao ya kisiasa.
Uhusiano huu unaweza kuwa msingi muhimu wa maendeleo ya kisiasa ya baadaye, kwani yanampa mgombea nafasi ya kujifunza, kupata msaada wa kiushauri, na kujenga sifa nzuri ndani ya jamii.
Kuzingatia maadili ya uongozi wa kweli
Wakati mwingine, kipindi cha kusubiri rufaa kinaweza kutoa changamoto ya kudumisha maadili ya kweli ya uongozi, hasa pale ambapo mgombea anakutana na hali zinazohatarisha imani yake.
Ni muhimu kwa wagombea kuendelea kujiimarisha na kuthibitisha uadilifu wao, hata katika hali ngumu, kwa kuonyesha dhamira ya dhati ya kuwa kiongozi wa kipekee anayeheshimu sheria na utaratibu.
Kwa kuwa mfano mzuri, wagombea wanaweza kujenga picha chanya itakayowasaidia siku zijazo, kwani wananchi hujenga imani kwa wale wanaoonyesha uthabiti na uaminifu bila kuyumbishwa na changamoto.
Uadilifu ni msingi wa uongozi bora na hata kama mgombea hatashinda rufaa, jamii itamkumbuka kwa msimamo wake thabiti.
Takwimu za Shirika la Utafiti wa Maadili ya Uongozi (SOMU) mwaka 2022, zinaonyesha asilimia 55 ya wapigakura huwa na uwezekano mkubwa wa kumuunga mkono mgombea ambaye anaonyesha uadilifu, hata baada ya kushindwa katika chaguzi za awali.
a4577.en:
What candidates should bear in mind while awaiting the appeal decision

Summary:
- The appeals process is an important part of the democratic system, giving those who believe they have been wronged an opportunity to seek justice.

Dar es Salaam. Calm, patience and a readiness to accept the outcome are three important things that should guide candidates for leadership positions during this period of waiting for the results of appeals.
In this period, the heart should be steady and the mind should remain calm, because their fate lies in the hands of the institutions and authorities responsible for making the final decision.

Valuing the legal process
The appeals process is an important part of the democratic system, giving those who believe they have been wronged an opportunity to seek justice.
On that basis, candidates should understand and appreciate that the process is intended to bring transparency and fairness to the entire electoral process.

Having patience
In today's world, patience has become rare; everyone wants quick answers.
However, during the appeals process, candidates should remember that correct answers take time.
According to statistics from the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), most appeals are decided within a period of less than one week, but this also depends on the weight of the arguments in each appeal.
Exercising patience helps candidates avoid regret and unrest, while respecting the time required for each stage of the process.

Preparing for any outcome
Not knowing what lies ahead can be psychologically challenging for many candidates.
A study by the Tanzania Political Research Organisation in 2021 showed that 40 percent of candidates who were rejected by electoral commissions fell into depression after their appeals failed.
It is important, then, for candidates to have an attitude of accepting any outcome so that they can get on with their lives, knowing that a leadership position is not the end of the world.

Setting out future strategies
This waiting period can be used wisely to reflect on long-term strategies.
If you do not succeed through the appeal, candidates should ask themselves what comes next; having a plan for the future is part of taking control of their lives and helps reduce the psychological impact.
This has been seen with many candidates who left political processes and devoted themselves to other social activities, a step that has helped contribute to development in the community.

Being an example to your followers
In this difficult period, a candidate's followers are filled with enthusiasm and great expectations.
Statistics from 2019 from the Police Force show that 60 percent of the violence reported during the local government elections was caused by supporters who were dissatisfied with the results of their candidates' appeals.
Candidates have a duty to be a good example to their followers by guiding them to respect the law and to wait calmly, a state of affairs that can also help maintain peace and calm in the community.

Observing ethics and civility in words and deeds
While waiting, candidates are advised to avoid statements that cause division and hatred in society.
A candidate should use civil language, representing respect and trustworthiness towards all.
Research by the University of Dar es Salaam (UDSM) in 2021 found that candidates who build a positive image in society through their words and deeds have a greater chance of obtaining lasting support even after the election.

Putting one's mind to other development activities
Instead of sitting and waiting without doing anything, candidates can involve themselves in various community activities.
Research shows that 45 percent of candidates who involve themselves in volunteer activities in the community increased their support in future elections, according to the international aid and development agency USAID.
This demonstrates that engaging in other community matters not only helps them forget the challenges of the election, but also gives them an opportunity to remain close to their community.

Seeking professional advice
Sometimes the stress arising from uncertainty can overwhelm a candidate.
Professional psychological counselling can help a candidate have a better outlook during the waiting period.
The World Health Organization (WHO) indicates that 15 percent of people who take part in politics have high levels of stress, especially while waiting for important results such as these.
These professional services can help a candidate find the strength to continue on the political journey or to take another direction in life.

Learning from the process
Every stage in politics carries a lesson, and the period of waiting for an appeal is a good opportunity to learn.
Candidates can analyse their strengths and weaknesses, assessing where they went wrong and where they did well.
Research from the Centre for Democracy and Development in 2022 shows that 70 percent of candidates who went through appeals came back with firmer plans and better strategies for taking part in future elections.
This means that using this time for learning can be a good way of preparing for coming challenges.
Waiting for the results of an appeal is not an easy thing, but it is an important part of the political journey.
It is a time that requires endurance, wisdom and a readiness to accept any outcome.
By understanding and respecting the appeals process, valuing patience, being an example to their followers, and preparing for the next steps, candidates can remain steady and continue to have hope for the community they want to lead.
The democratic system enables citizens to seek justice, and likewise it requires the responsibility of having discipline and integrity.

Strengthening relationships with key stakeholders
In politics, relationships and a network of stakeholders are an important tool that can help a candidate strengthen themselves politically even in challenging circumstances.
While waiting for the results of an appeal, it is an appropriate opportunity for candidates to build and maintain relationships with political leaders, activists, and influential members of the community.
Research conducted by the Institute of Political and Democratic Affairs (TPDI) in 2021 found that 35 percent of candidates who cooperated with key stakeholders obtained a good chance of gaining support over a long period, despite the challenges they encountered during the election.
In this waiting period, candidates should use their time wisely by taking part in community activities that build them up and include them in political networks.
These relationships can be an important foundation for future political development, since they give a candidate the chance to learn, to receive advisory support, and to build a good reputation within the community.

Observing the ethics of true leadership
Sometimes the period of waiting for an appeal can present the challenge of maintaining the true ethics of leadership, especially where a candidate encounters situations that endanger their convictions.
It is important for candidates to continue to strengthen themselves and to demonstrate their integrity, even in difficult circumstances, by showing a sincere determination to be an exceptional leader who respects the law and due process.
By being a good example, candidates can build a positive image that will help them in the days to come, because citizens build trust in those who show steadfastness and integrity without being shaken by challenges.
Integrity is the foundation of good leadership, and even if a candidate does not win the appeal, the community will remember them for their firm stand.
Statistics from the Leadership Ethics Research Organisation (SOMU) in 2022 show that 55 percent of voters are more likely to support a candidate who shows integrity, even after losing in earlier elections.

a4708.t:
A primeira entrega foi de 150 toneladas, de um total de 1.500 toneladas, que irão para 2.450 famílias dedicadas à criação e tratamento de gado na Faixa de Gaza, informou hoje a Organização das Nações Unidas para a Alimentação e a Agricultura (FAO).
"Cada animal que morre provoca impactos duradouros, já que a sua substituição é cara e praticamente impossível devido às restrições às importações", explicou o diretor da unidade da FAO na Cisjordânia e na Faixa de Gaza, Ciro Fiorillo, citado pelas agências internacionais.
A organização pretende entregar, numa primeira fase, um total de 1.500 toneladas de forragem, o suficiente para produzir e fornecer leite durante 50 dias a todas as crianças em Gaza com menos de 10 anos, o que já permite atingir cerca de 20% das necessidades diárias mínimas recomendadas pela Organização Mundial da Saúde (OMS) em termos de calorias.
Esta é a primeira vez, desde a escalada das hostilidades no pequeno e sobrepovoado enclave palestiniano, que entram forragens em Gaza, tendo as restrições "causado o colapso das cadeias de valor agroalimentares, contribuindo para a rápida deterioração da segurança alimentar", referiu a organização.
Desde o início do conflito, em 07 de Outubro de 2023, 55% dos animais relacionados com o fornecimento de carne e de leite na Faixa de Gaza foram abatidos, consumidos ou perdidos e, em março, restavam apenas cerca de 30.000, adiantou a FAO.
"Ao garantir a disponibilidade de forragem, podemos apoiar a sobrevivência e a reprodução do gado e fornecer alimentos essenciais, frescos e nutritivos, mesmo durante os conflitos", explicou Fiorillo.
A FAO comprometeu-se ainda a expandir a sua ajuda fornecendo "apoio agrícola crucial para restaurar a disponibilidade de alimentos altamente nutritivos, evitar o colapso total do setor, preservar os meios de subsistência restantes e reduzir a fome aguda e a desnutrição".
A comunidade internacional tem apelado em diversas ocasiões a Israel para que permita a entrada de uma maior quantidade de ajuda humanitária para a Faixa de Gaza, especialmente no norte do enclave, onde a situação é mais grave e se estima que ali vivam cerca de 300.000 pessoas.
O conflito em curso na Faixa de Gaza foi desencadeado pelo ataque do grupo islamita Hamas em solo israelita de 07 de Outubro de 2023, que causou cerca de 1.200 mortos e duas centenas de reféns, segundo as autoridades israelitas.
Desde então, Israel lançou uma ofensiva na Faixa de Gaza que provocou mais de 33.000 mortos, segundo o Hamas, que governa o pequeno enclave palestiniano desde 2007.
A retaliação israelita está a provocar uma grave crise humanitária em Gaza, com mais de 1,1 milhões de pessoas numa "situação de fome catastrófica" que já está a fazer vítimas - "o número mais elevado alguma vez registado" pela ONU em estudos sobre segurança alimentar no mundo.
A população da Faixa de Gaza confronta-se com o colapso dos hospitais, surtos de doenças e escassez de água potável, alimentos, medicamentos e eletricidade.
A ofensiva israelita também tem destruído a maioria das infraestruturas de Gaza e perto de dois milhões de pessoas foram forçadas a abandonar as suas casas, ou seja, a quase totalidade dos 2,3 milhões de habitantes do enclave.
a4708.en:
FAO. UN agency begins sending animal fodder to Gaza

The first delivery was 150 tonnes, out of a total of 1,500 tonnes, which will go to 2,450 families dedicated to raising and caring for livestock in the Gaza Strip, the United Nations Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) reported today.

"Every animal that dies causes lasting impacts, since replacing it is expensive and practically impossible because of the restrictions on imports," explained the director of the FAO unit in the West Bank and the Gaza Strip, Ciro Fiorillo, quoted by international news agencies.

The organisation intends to deliver, in a first phase, a total of 1,500 tonnes of fodder, enough to produce and supply milk for 50 days to all children in Gaza under 10 years of age, which already makes it possible to reach about 20% of the minimum daily requirements recommended by the World Health Organization (WHO) in terms of calories.

This is the first time, since the escalation of hostilities in the small and overcrowded Palestinian enclave, that fodder has entered Gaza, the restrictions having "caused the collapse of the agri-food value chains, contributing to the rapid deterioration of food security", the organisation said.

Since the start of the conflict on 7 October 2023, 55% of the animals connected with the supply of meat and milk in the Gaza Strip have been slaughtered, consumed or lost and, in March, only about 30,000 remained, the FAO added.

"By ensuring the availability of fodder, we can support the survival and reproduction of livestock and provide essential, fresh and nutritious food, even during conflicts," explained Fiorillo.

The FAO further committed itself to expanding its aid by providing "crucial agricultural support to restore the availability of highly nutritious foods, avoid the total collapse of the sector, preserve the remaining livelihoods and reduce acute hunger and malnutrition".

The international community has appealed on various occasions to Israel to allow a greater quantity of humanitarian aid to enter the Gaza Strip, especially in the north of the enclave, where the situation is most serious and where an estimated 300,000 people are thought to live.

The ongoing conflict in the Gaza Strip was triggered by the attack by the Islamist group Hamas on Israeli soil on 7 October 2023, which caused about 1,200 deaths and two hundred hostages, according to the Israeli authorities.

Since then, Israel has launched an offensive in the Gaza Strip that has caused more than 33,000 deaths, according to Hamas, which has governed the small Palestinian enclave since 2007.

The Israeli retaliation is causing a serious humanitarian crisis in Gaza, with more than 1.1 million people in a "catastrophic hunger situation" that is already claiming victims - "the highest number ever recorded" by the UN in studies on food security in the world.

The population of the Gaza Strip is facing the collapse of hospitals, outbreaks of disease and shortages of drinking water, food, medicines and electricity.

The Israeli offensive has also destroyed most of Gaza's infrastructure and close to two million people have been forced to abandon their homes, that is, almost the entirety of the enclave's 2.3 million inhabitants.

a4765.t:
The road, which had initially raised hopes for better infrastructure and ease of access, has now become a source of frustration as severe flooding plagues the area.
Motorists and commuters along the busy Udeagbara Bypass Road in Ahiaba Umueze Owuala in Osisioma Ngwa Local Government Area of Abia State during the weekend were stranded, owing to a gridlock caused by flood in the aftermath of a heavy downpour.
SaharaReporters learnt that the road was recently commissioned by Governor Alex Otti.
“Abia State Governor, Dr. Alex Otti, has continued to match words with action with the formal commissioning of three-newly reconstructed roads in Aba.
“The roads are Udeagbala Road, Umuimo Road and MCC/Old Express Road.
“Governor Otti described the three roads as strategic, saying that the Udeagbala and Umuimo roads in particular are more or less alternative from the Enugu-Port Harcourt Expressway into the busy Aba-Owerri Road and to Abia State University Teaching Hospital (ABSUTH) road, while the MCC/Old Express Road would boost the economy of Aba, the commercial nerve centre of the State,” a statement by Kazie Uko, the governor’s former Chief Press Secretary had read during the commissioning.
However, few months after the road was opened, residents have expressed deep concerns over the failure of the newly rehabilitated road and drainage system.
The road, which had initially raised hopes for better infrastructure and ease of access, has now become a source of frustration as severe flooding plagues the area.
It was learnt that the community, which houses the Abia State Teaching Hospital, is facing significant challenges as the drainage system, meant to alleviate flooding, has failed to perform its intended purpose.
As a result, residents are now left grappling with constant waterlogging, making it difficult to carry out their daily activities.
Many have reported having to wait until floodwaters subside before leaving their homes, especially after rainfalls.
In a live video shared by a community member, Possible Nwaohamuo on Sunday, he highlighted the extent of the problem.
In the video, Nwaohamuo made the appeal to the state government, urging for immediate intervention.
He pointed out that the floodwaters from the failed drainage system have not only taken over homes but have also severely affected schools and places of worship in the area.
“The flooding is a disaster for our community,” Nwaohamuo said during his broadcast.
“We can no longer go about our daily activities in peace. Our children cannot go to school, and our places of worship are submerged. We need the government to come to our rescue.
“Despite the rehabilitation project being relatively new, its failure has raised questions about the quality of work done and the long-term sustainability of such projects.”

a4783.t:
Le président de la République du Burundi, Evariste Ndayishimiye a tenu, le vendredi 28 mars 2025, une séance de moralisation animée à l’intention des opérateurs économiques. Il les a interpellés à travailler dans l’unité, la transparence et l’honnêteté.
Le président Evariste Ndayishimiye a d’abord exhorté les opérateurs économiques et les investisseurs burundais à adopter une vision d’avenir. Il les a appelés à privilégier la création d’entreprises de production afin de proposer des biens destinés à l’exportation, plutôt que de se limiter aux importations. Il a insisté sur le fait que les Burundais doivent tirer profit de la paix et de la sécurité qui règnent actuellement dans le pays, des éléments fondamentaux pour le développement. Il a également rappelé que le progrès du Burundi repose sur l’engagement de ses citoyens.
Couper court avec les pratiques de fraudes fiscales
Le chef de l’Etat a poursuivi en interpellant les opérateurs économiques à ne pas compter uniquement sur l’aide étrangère, insistant ainsi sur l’importance du travail collectif et de l’unité pour bâtir une économie forte. Par ailleurs, il a lancé un appel à l’ensemble des acteurs économiques à renoncer aux pratiques frauduleuses dans le domaine fiscal, soulignant l’impact négatif de ces dernières sur la croissance du pays.
Le numéro Un burundais, a également interpellé les opérateurs économiques sur l’importance de s’acquitter de leurs impôts et taxes conformément à la loi, soulignant que ces contributions sont essentielles au développement du pays. Selon lui, les recettes fiscales permettent notamment de financer la production d’électricité, l’achat de médicaments, le développement des infrastructures et bien d’autres secteurs vitaux. Il les a également exhortés à renforcer les chaînes de valeur afin de faciliter l’accès aux matières premières et de promouvoir un développement collectif durable.
Le président Ndayishimiye a également déploré certaines pratiques visant à déstabiliser l’économie nationale. Selon lui, bien que les devises soient disponibles en quantité suffisante dans le pays, certains Burundais manœuvrent pour empêcher leur entrée dans la Banque centrale et les banques commerciales. Il a ainsi appelé à un changement de mentalité, encourageant un esprit patriotique axé sur le développement du pays en affirmant que le Burundi ne peut prospérer qu’avec l’implication active de ses citoyens ; à défaut, il risquerait de sombrer dans le déclin économique.
La problématique des devises et l’appel au patriotisme économique
Face aux défis liés à la disponibilité des devises, le directeur général de l’ADB (Agence de Développement du Burundi), Révérien Nizigiyimana invite les opérateurs économiques burundais à devenir des producteurs de devises plutôt que de se contenter d’en être demandeurs. Il les encourage à adopter une vision plus large, en s’intéressant non seulement au marché local mais aussi au marché extérieur. Il souligne l’importance de l’économie d’échelle, en suggérant aux entrepreneurs d’unir leurs capitaux afin de créer de grandes entreprises compétitives à l’échelle internationale.
Olivier Suguru, président de la CFCIB (Chambre fédéral du commerce et d’industri du Burundi), a quant lui salué la volonté du Chef de l’Etat d’encourager les opérateurs économiques, comme en témoignent les rencontres qu’il organise pour renforcer le dialogue entre les secteurs public et privé. Et de rappeller que la CFCIB a pour mission d’intervenir en cas de violations des droits du secteur privé et non de résoudre les litiges des membres ou opérateurs du secteur privé ayant enfreint la loi. Selon lui, tout contrevenant doit répondre de ses actes devant les juridictions compétentes.
La fraude fiscale crée un déséquilibre dans l’économie nationale
M. Suguru dénonce avec fermeté les opérateurs économiques qui se livrent à la fraude douanière et fiscale. Il les exhorte à mettre fin à ces mauvais pratiques, qui freinent l’élargissement de l’assiette fiscale et entravent le développement du pays. Selon lui, la fraude fiscale entraîne l’évasion de l’impôt sur le revenu, créant ainsi un déséquilibre dans l’économie nationale et le commerce. Il souligne également que cette fraude s’opère souvent en chaîne, impliquant certains agents des douanes et de la police, et déplore vivement cette situation. Il appelle chacun à dénoncer ces pratiques nuisibles au développement du pays.
Par ailleurs, la CFCIB demande des mesures urgentes pour améliorer la disponibilité des devises et assainir l’environnement des affaires au Burundi. En effet, les opérateurs économiques peinent à obtenir des devises en banque et se tournent vers le marché parallèle, une situation préoccupante qui nécessite une solution rapide et efficace. Olivier Suguru avertit que cette problématique pourrait avoir de graves conséquences sur l’économie nationale, notamment en raison du calcul des impôts basé sur le taux de change de la BRB (Banque de la République du Burundi).
Laurent Mpundunziza
a4783.en:
The President of the Republic of Burundi, Evariste Ndayishimiye, held a lively moralisation session on Friday 28 March 2025 for economic operators. He called on them to work in unity, transparency and honesty.

President Evariste Ndayishimiye first urged Burundian economic operators and investors to adopt a forward-looking vision. He called on them to prioritise the creation of production companies in order to offer goods destined for export, rather than limiting themselves to imports. He insisted that Burundians must take advantage of the peace and security currently prevailing in the country, which are fundamental elements for development. He also recalled that Burundi's progress rests on the commitment of its citizens.

Putting an end to tax fraud practices

The Head of State went on to call on economic operators not to rely solely on foreign aid, thus insisting on the importance of collective work and unity in building a strong economy. He also made an appeal to all economic actors to renounce fraudulent practices in the fiscal domain, underlining their negative impact on the country's growth.

Burundi's number one also called on economic operators to pay their taxes and duties in accordance with the law, stressing that these contributions are essential to the country's development. According to him, tax revenues make it possible in particular to finance electricity production, the purchase of medicines, the development of infrastructure and many other vital sectors. He also urged them to strengthen value chains in order to facilitate access to raw materials and to promote sustainable collective development.

President Ndayishimiye also deplored certain practices aimed at destabilising the national economy. According to him, although foreign currency is available in sufficient quantity in the country, some Burundians manoeuvre to prevent it from entering the Central Bank and the commercial banks. He thus called for a change of mentality, encouraging a patriotic spirit focused on the country's development, stating that Burundi can only prosper with the active involvement of its citizens; failing that, it risks sinking into economic decline.

The currency problem and the call for economic patriotism

Faced with the challenges linked to the availability of foreign currency, the Director General of the ADB (Burundi Development Agency), Révérien Nizigiyimana, invites Burundian economic operators to become producers of foreign currency rather than merely requesting it. He encourages them to adopt a broader vision, taking an interest not only in the local market but also in the foreign market. He stresses the importance of economies of scale, suggesting that entrepreneurs pool their capital in order to create large companies that are competitive at the international level.

Olivier Suguru, president of the CFCIB (Federal Chamber of Commerce and Industry of Burundi), for his part welcomed the Head of State's willingness to encourage economic operators, as shown by the meetings he organises to strengthen dialogue between the public and private sectors. He recalled that the CFCIB's mission is to intervene in cases of violations of the rights of the private sector, and not to resolve disputes involving private-sector members or operators who have broken the law. According to him, any offender must answer for their acts before the competent courts.

Tax fraud creates an imbalance in the national economy

Mr Suguru firmly denounces economic operators who engage in customs and tax fraud. He urges them to put an end to these bad practices, which hinder the broadening of the tax base and impede the country's development. According to him, tax fraud leads to the evasion of income tax, thereby creating an imbalance in the national economy and in trade. He also stresses that this fraud often operates as a chain, involving certain customs and police officers, and he deeply deplores this situation. He calls on everyone to denounce these practices that are harmful to the country's development.

Moreover, the CFCIB is calling for urgent measures to improve the availability of foreign currency and to clean up the business environment in Burundi. Indeed, economic operators are struggling to obtain foreign currency from banks and are turning to the parallel market, a worrying situation that requires a rapid and effective solution. Olivier Suguru warns that this problem could have serious consequences for the national economy, notably because of the calculation of taxes based on the exchange rate of the BRB (Bank of the Republic of Burundi).

Laurent Mpundunziza

a4802.t:
Grâce à une contribution de 124 millions de dollars de l’Agence américaine pour le développement international (USAID), le Burkina va pouvoir faire face à une crise humanitaire exacerbée par l’insécurité croissante.
Au Burkina Faso, le gouvernement combat depuis plusieurs années des groupes terroristes qui sévissent sur une grande partie du territoire, provoquant le dénuement de nombreuses personnes.
Le Programme alimentaire mondial (PAM) a déclaré mardi avoir apporté une aide vitale à un million de personnes touchées par « une crise humanitaire complexe » au Burkina Faso. Cette assistance a été rendue possible grâce à une contribution de 124 millions de dollars de l’Agence américaine pour le développement international (USAID), représentant 70% de toutes les contributions des donateurs au bureau du PAM pour le Burkina Faso en 2024.
Cette contribution comprend 99 millions de dollars comme aide alimentaire d’urgence et 25 millions de dollars pour le Service aérien humanitaire des Nations Unies (UNHAS), a précisé l’agence onusienne dans un communiqué. « À une époque de crise mondiale croissante, ce soutien indéfectible a permis au PAM d’atteindre les populations dans le besoin dans les endroits difficiles d’accès du Burkina Faso », s’est réjoui Sory Ouane, représentant du PAM au Burkina Faso. « Nous sommes profondément reconnaissants du partenariat et de la confiance que le gouvernement américain nous a accordés », a-t-il ajouté.
En 2024, on estime que 2,7 millions de personnes – soit 12 % de la population – ont eu besoin d’une aide alimentaire immédiate pendant la période de soudure de juin à août, selon l’analyse de la sécurité alimentaire du Cadre harmonisé de mars 2024.
Grâce au financement du gouvernement américain, le PAM a pu venir en aide à plus d’un million de femmes, d’hommes et d’enfants vulnérables face à l’insécurité alimentaire et à la malnutrition.
Le PAM gère également le Service aérien humanitaire des Nations Unies (UNHAS), qui permet le transport sûr et fiable des travailleurs humanitaires et des articles de secours vers des zones reculées et difficiles d’accès au Burkina Faso.
Entre janvier et septembre 2024, près de 15 000 travailleurs humanitaires ont été transportés et plus de 500 tonnes de fournitures de secours ont été livrées par l’intermédiaire de l’UNHAS, garantissant que les services essentiels parviennent aux communautés les plus isolées.
ODL/Sf/ac/APA
a4802.en:
Thanks to a contribution of 124 million dollars from the United States Agency for International Development (USAID), Burkina will be able to cope with a humanitarian crisis exacerbated by growing insecurity.

In Burkina Faso, the government has for several years been fighting terrorist groups that are active across a large part of the territory, causing destitution for many people.

The World Food Programme (WFP) said on Tuesday that it had provided life-saving assistance to one million people affected by "a complex humanitarian crisis" in Burkina Faso. This assistance was made possible thanks to a contribution of 124 million dollars from the United States Agency for International Development (USAID), representing 70% of all donor contributions to the WFP office for Burkina Faso in 2024.

This contribution comprises 99 million dollars as emergency food assistance and 25 million dollars for the United Nations Humanitarian Air Service (UNHAS), the UN agency specified in a statement. "At a time of growing global crisis, this unwavering support has enabled WFP to reach people in need in hard-to-reach places in Burkina Faso," welcomed Sory Ouane, WFP Representative in Burkina Faso. "We are deeply grateful for the partnership and the trust that the American government has placed in us," he added.

In 2024, an estimated 2.7 million people - or 12% of the population - needed immediate food assistance during the lean season from June to August, according to the food security analysis of the Cadre Harmonise of March 2024.

Thanks to funding from the American government, WFP was able to come to the aid of more than one million vulnerable women, men and children facing food insecurity and malnutrition.

WFP also manages the United Nations Humanitarian Air Service (UNHAS), which allows the safe and reliable transport of humanitarian workers and relief items to remote and hard-to-reach areas of Burkina Faso.

Between January and September 2024, nearly 15,000 humanitarian workers were transported and more than 500 tonnes of relief supplies were delivered through UNHAS, ensuring that essential services reach the most isolated communities.

ODL/Sf/ac/APA

a5041.t:
Fortune News | Feb 23,2019
As federal authorities eagerly anticipate the potential billion-dollar International Monetary Fund (IMF) package, a team from the Fund conducted a series of meetings in the capital over the past week that could significantly determine the country's economic fate.
The staff met with Mamo Mihretu, governor of the National Bank of Ethiopia (NBE); Ahmed Shide and Eyob Tekalegen (PhD), minister and state minister for Finance; Abie Sano, president of the state-owned Commercial Bank of Ethiopia (CBE); Fistum Assefa (PhD), minister of Planning & Development; Teklewold Atnafu, senior monetary policy advisor; and, Girma Birru, chief macroeconomic advisor to the Prime Minister.
The team's visit is part of ongoing discussions, a follow-up to the one held back in October. A staff-level agreement is expected to be reached before the IMF Board approves a program. However, no deal was reported until our press time on Saturday evening.
Ethiopia's request for financial assistance from the IMF to address food security, humanitarian needs, post-conflict reconstruction, and combatting high inflation is contingent on a staff-level agreement requiring structural economic reforms. Its economic future hinges on a successful negotiation with the IMF, whose directors have signalled their interest in providing up to 3.5 billion dollars in loans.
"Discussions took place and will continue to occur," Governor Mamo told Fortune, declining to comment on details of the discussions.
Tobias N. Rasmussen, IMF's resident representative in Ethiopia, also declined to comment.
"We cannot answer these questions as negotiations are ongoing," he responded by email to questions Fortune forwarded to his office.
However, people informed of the ongoing talks point to the liberalisation of the forex regime, discipline over off-budget spending, tax reforms, and the restructuring of high debts held by state enterprises as contentious issues between Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed's (PhD) administration and the IMF. The IMF team argue that these are crucial steps to restore macroeconomic stability.
Experts say that while loans and debt restructuring offer a lifeline, implementing the reforms the IMF pushes will be critical to achieving sustainable economic growth. For a country currently juggling foreign currency sufficient to cover only three weeks of imports, with over 20 million people in need of humanitarian assistance, and security concerns in several parts of the country impeding economic productivity, they pose the question, what next?
According to Governor Mamo, the central bank is committed to maintaining stable prices with a single-digit inflation rate, promoting financial inclusion and restructuring the central bank under a new proclamation soon, regardless of external support. He said the National Bank of Ethiopia's three-year strategic plan guides these actions.
The three-year plan involves transitioning from a monetary policy targeting aggregate money to a price-based system, relying on open market operations and interest rates as key initiatives. The shift aligns with the recommendations often prescribed by IMF's experts for debt-burdened economies seeking assistance from multilateral banks. It also includes measures such as promoting market operations, enhancing interbank forex and money markets, reviewing current and capital account restrictions, and addressing the disparities between official and parallel foreign exchange rates.
The potential IMF financial assistance to Ethiopia carries significant implications beyond immediate relief, as it is a prerequisite for successful debt relief under the Group of 20's Common Framework mechanism. Bilateral creditors have set a deadline of March 31 for an agreement with the IMF, enabling Ethiopia to benefit from a debt suspension agreement from November. An IMF program is vital to the debt restructuring process under the Common Framework (CF).
Ethiopia's application for debt restructuring was filed in February 2021, with talks beginning five months later. On September 16, 2021, a creditor committee comprising 12 countries, co-chaired by China and France, was formed. The committee includes Ethiopia's major creditors, such as Denmark, France, Italy, Korea, Japan, and the Saudi Fund for Development. China is the major bilateral non-Paris Club creditor, claiming 30pc of the total external debt stock.
The evolution of Ethiopia's external debt over the four years since 2019 has been marked by slight fluctuations, revealing the authorities' caution to borrowing and debt management during economic uncertainties and aid freezes due to wars. The external debt witnessed modest adjustments — rising to 29.4 billion dollars in 2020/21 from 28.8 billion dollars the year before. It then dipped to 27.9 billion dollars in 2021/22, making a minor recovery to 28 billion dollars last year. As of September 30, 2023, the figure slightly lowered to 27.7 billion dollars.
Ethiopia's external debt structure is characterised by its interest rate composition, which mixes fixed and variable rates, with a portion being interest-free. Over recent years, there has been a noticeable tilt towards fixed interest rates, showing the authorities' preference for predictability in debt service costs, which are believed to reach four billion dollars in two years, according to projections the UNDP made.
There has been a significant channelling of funds into sectors deemed essential for growth and development. The government has prioritised investment areas in agriculture, transport and communications, electricity, gas and steam, and water supply.
The authorities depended on a mix of official creditors for the country's financial needs. Multilateral institutions like the International Development Association (IDA) and the African Development Bank (AfDB) remain significant sources of concessional loans, which offer lower interest rates and extended repayment terms. The authorities view the benefits of concessional loans — lower interest rates and more extended repayment periods — as critical in maintaining debt sustainability. However, non-concessional and commercial loans introduce a layer of burden, stressing the need for meticulous debt management to prevent less favourable loan terms from undermining the country's financial stability.
The external debt stock, with 19pc owed to private creditors, has attracted increased scrutiny from foreign bondholders. The scrutiny intensified when the country failed to make a 33 million dollar coupon payment in December.
An IMF program entails more than transitioning to a market-based exchange rate system; it requires comprehensive macroeconomic stability. Reforms to address current account deficits, achieve debt sustainability, recalibrate the balance of payments, reduce inflation to single digits, and ensure debt sustainability are first in line. A macroeconomist, speaking anonymously, likened the IMF program to an ambulance providing immediate assistance, with long-term health dependent on sustained attention to overall well-being.
"Tough but essential measures are what the program offers," he said.
The macroeconomist praised the central bank's current orientation and urged strong, sound, and resilient reforms. According to the macroeconomist, countries benefiting from IMF programs must leverage the potential credit facility to address structural economic imbalances effectively.
"It's timely and encouraging," he told Fortune.
While forecasts about the economic implications of an IMF agreement have to wait until the specific deals are known, the potential benefits of further debt restructuring agreements for lifting temporary debt burdens are not up for debate.
The inevitable devaluation of the Birr has been a topic of discussion, partly driven by the IMF's emphasis on liberal exchange markets and the Prime Minister's hinting at forthcoming reforms. Prime Minister Abiy recently likened reforms to a dentist pulling out a tooth, signalling the need for strict measures. The IMF's support for Ethiopia's economic reform agenda is contingent upon the administration's political will to implement enabling reforms. The initial reforms proposed in 2019 targeted a gradual transition to a flexible exchange rate regime to narrow the gap between the parallel and official markets.
People familiar with the ongoing talks say Ethiopia's authorities have agreed on the reform measures to be taken in principle; the bone of contention with the IMF is over extended time and phased implementations deals they call "back-loaded." In the experts' parlance, the IMF team insisted on "front-loaded" deals, meaning the authorities should take reform measures immediately after programs have been agreed upon.
Economist Atlaw Alemu (PhD) downplayed the significance of either a slight currency devaluation or a significant shift in exchange rate policy for the main economy. He views the economic turmoil as stemming from deeper systemic failures rather than exchange rate policies. Recalling past devaluations, including a 15pc drop six years ago, Atlaw noted that such actions did little to improve export performance or bolster foreign currency reserves.
"Exchange rate policy is a smaller element of the country's economic problems," he told Fortune.
According to the economist, the agricultural export sector, reliant on imports for inputs like fertiliser and seeds, will struggle with higher costs regardless of exchange rate adjustments. Unlike countries like China, which benefit from currency devaluation due to higher exports, Ethiopia's productivity levels have not improved significantly. Atlaw suggested that while the IMF program could somewhat relieve debt burdens, it may not address the root causes of the economic malaise.
"A path to a little debt relief is all the IMF could offer," Atlaw said.

a5315.t:
It was an auspicious occasion when some stakeholders of Liberia’s agriculture and food system recently deliberated on the successes and challenges of the nation’s agriculture in observance of the World Food Day celebration.
The program which aimed to highlight the accomplishments of agriculture and the food system was organized by Agrotech, a youth focused organization.
World Food Day is observed every year on October 16 to highlight the achievements of agriculture and the food system globally.
The event brought together key stakeholders, including farmers, the private sector actors, young entrepreneurs in the agricultural sector to share their perspectives on the way to promote food security in the country, particularly in line with the current National Agriculture Development Plan for Liberia.
Reflecting the progress made thus far in improving food security and the challenges that still need attention, the food system actors, some who served as panelists during the event underscored the need for a transformative agriculture.
The panelists mentioned the need for the government to exert more efforts to address pertinent issues that still confronts the country’s agriculture and food system.
They outlined ensuring women access to land, improving on extension services, improving on access to finance and the provision of adequate inputs among others as some critical issues.
Accordingly, the panelists said that addressing those issues will inspire more young farmers and agripreneurs to set out in exploring opportunities in the agriculture and agribusiness sector.
They also use the opportunity to explain their organization contributions toward food security in Liberia over the past year.
Hawa Dunor Varney, Executive Director for the Women In Agriculture said that women contribute immensely to the food system in Liberia and as such there is need for the government to continue to create the enabling environment to improve farming.
According to her as an organization, considering the difficulties women experienced in access to land they are working to create awareness around the issue.
“We are providing the skills and knowledge as well as providing them the education on business knowledge to make agriculture a business. We are also providing literacy education as part of our programs so that the women can go out and seek for opportunities,” she said.
As an organization we advocate women access to land in communities to be able to provide land to grow their food.
Hired Lankah, of Nimba Venture, a snail farmer, explained that his organization is working to change the minds set of the young people about agriculture.
“We provide not just food security but also alternative livelihood. I try to make the young people understand that agriculture requires developing the proper mindset to succeed,” he said.
He mentioned that there are a lot of challenges that still confront snail farming and so they’re supporting young people who don't have the starting capital.
Neemu Barcom of the Farmer Union Network of Liberia explained that her organization has been very much busy addressing post harvest losses in the food sector.
“We also worked to train farmers in the past for rice cultivation, adding that her organization currently works to revamp the coffee sector.
According to her, the program aims to train the farmers in improved coffee cultivation to improve incomes.
Barcom said that though the project is yet to provide equipment, farmers are trained in harvest and processing.
According to her, for the first time, under the program farmers were able to export some quantities of coffee to Europe.
“The farmers are very much excited about the program as more women and youths are now getting involved,” she explained.

région fait face. Il a mis en exergue les obstacles spécifiques à l’Afrique de
l’Ouest, en particulier au sein de l’Uemoa, à l’occasion des assemblées
annuelles du groupe de la Banque mondiale et du Fonds monétaire international
(Fmi) qui ont réuni des responsables de banques centrales, des ministres des
Finances, des leaders du secteur privé et des universitaires. 
Lors d’une réunion de haut niveau consacrée à l’Uemoa, le gouverneur de la Bceao a insisté sur la nécessaire stabilité macroéconomique pour soutenir la croissance régionale malgré les chocs externes. «La résilience de notre économie repose sur une politique fiscale et monétaire adaptée, notamment dans un contexte de volatilité économique mondiale», a-t-il affirmé, évoquant les répercussions du changement climatique, de la dette et de l’insécurité dans la région. Les discussions ont notamment porté sur l’augmentation de l’endettement des pays africains. Selon les dernières données, la dette extérieure publique en Afrique subsaharienne a quadruplé en moins de deux décennies, passant de 108 milliards de dollars en 2006 à 462 milliards de dollars en 2022. Ce poids de la dette limite la capacité des États à financer des projets de développement et rend les économies de la région vulnérables aux fluctuations des taux d’intérêt mondiaux. « Il devient essentiel d’instaurer des mécanismes pour mieux gérer cette dette et réduire le risque de surendettement », a souligné Jean-Claude Kassi Brou. Face à ces contraintes budgétaires, il a proposé une meilleure coordination entre les institutions financières internationales et les institutions régionales, afin de mettre en place des instruments financiers innovants qui répondent aux besoins spécifiques des pays africains.
Dans une région où l’agriculture constitue le principal moteur de l’économie, le changement climatique a des effets dramatiques sur les moyens de subsistance et la sécurité alimentaire. Entre 1980 et 2022, les catastrophes climatiques ont affecté plus de 80 millions de personnes dans la zone Uemoa, selon les données fournies par la Bceao. Face à la situation, Jean-Claude Kassi Brou a affirmé que les variations climatiques influencent directement la croissance économique et accroissent les vulnérabilités en matière de santé et d’emploi. « Nous devons intensifier nos efforts pour intégrer des stratégies de résilience climatique dans nos politiques économiques », a-t-il proposé. Pour répondre à ce défi, le gouverneur appelle à une mobilisation de ressources internationales visant à financer des infrastructures résilientes et à renforcer les capacités locales pour atténuer les effets climatiques. L'autre sujet majeur abordé lors de ces assemblées annuelles est la stabilité sociopolitique de la région, mise à mal par la montée des conflits et la fragilité sécuritaire. Il est constaté une augmentation des dépenses militaires de l’Uemoa et cela pèse sur les budgets des États, au détriment des investissements dans le développement socio-économique. Le gouverneur a insisté sur la nécessité d'une approche équilibrée dans l'allocation des ressources publiques. « Une sécurité renforcée est essentielle pour protéger les infrastructures et encourager les investissements étrangers, mais elle ne doit pas compromettre le financement du développement social et économique », précise Jean-Claude Kassi Brou.
La
région doit également relever le défi de l'emploi pour sa population
majoritairement jeune. Jean-Claude Kassi Brou a souligné l'importance de
renforcer le capital humain et de créer des opportunités d’emploi adaptées aux
besoins du marché. « Le défi de l’emploi est urgent. Nous devons explorer des
stratégies qui favorisent l’insertion professionnelle des jeunes, notamment à
travers l'entrepreneuriat et la digitalisation », a-t-il indiqué, appelant à un
engagement accru des acteurs internationaux pour soutenir les initiatives
d’emploi dans les économies émergentes. Le gouverneur de la Bceao a insisté sur
la nécessité d’une action coordonnée et d'une coopération internationale
renforcée. Il a plaidé pour l’adaptation des instruments financiers mondiaux
aux spécificités des pays en développement. Les assemblées annuelles de la
Banque mondiale et du Fmi ont offert aux pays de la région une tribune pour
défendre leurs intérêts et promouvoir une vision de croissance inclusive et
durable■

La Nation Bénin...
At the annual meetings of the World Bank and the International Monetary Fund (IMF) held from 21 to 26 October in Washington, Jean-Claude Kassi Brou, Governor of the BCEAO, stressed economic priorities within the WAEMU area. Faced with growing indebtedness, climate risks, security and youth employment, he calls for strengthened cooperation to ensure the region's stability.

Economic stability is a challenge for West African countries. Facing the major international financial players in Washington, Jean-Claude Kassi Brou, Governor of the Central Bank of West African States (BCEAO), made heard the voice of the West African Economic and Monetary Union (WAEMU). Between rising debt, the effects of climate change and the employment crisis for a rapidly growing young population, the challenges are considerable. But for Jean-Claude Kassi Brou, one thing is clear: only strengthened global cooperation will make it possible to meet the challenges the region faces. He highlighted the obstacles specific to West Africa, particularly within WAEMU, on the occasion of the annual meetings of the World Bank Group and the International Monetary Fund (IMF), which brought together central bank officials, finance ministers, private-sector leaders and academics.

At a high-level meeting devoted to WAEMU, the BCEAO Governor insisted on the macroeconomic stability needed to support regional growth despite external shocks. "The resilience of our economy rests on appropriate fiscal and monetary policy, particularly in a context of global economic volatility," he stated, citing the repercussions of climate change, debt and insecurity in the region. The discussions notably addressed the rise in African countries' indebtedness. According to the latest data, public external debt in sub-Saharan Africa has quadrupled in less than two decades, rising from $108 billion in 2006 to $462 billion in 2022. This debt burden limits states' capacity to finance development projects and makes the region's economies vulnerable to fluctuations in global interest rates. "It is becoming essential to establish mechanisms to better manage this debt and reduce the risk of over-indebtedness," Jean-Claude Kassi Brou emphasised. Faced with these budgetary constraints, he proposed better coordination between international financial institutions and regional institutions, in order to put in place innovative financial instruments that respond to the specific needs of African countries.

In a region where agriculture is the main engine of the economy, climate change has dramatic effects on livelihoods and food security. Between 1980 and 2022, climate disasters affected more than 80 million people in the WAEMU zone, according to data provided by the BCEAO. Faced with this situation, Jean-Claude Kassi Brou stated that climate variations directly influence economic growth and increase vulnerabilities in health and employment. "We must step up our efforts to integrate climate resilience strategies into our economic policies," he proposed. To meet this challenge, the Governor calls for a mobilisation of international resources aimed at financing resilient infrastructure and strengthening local capacities to mitigate climate effects. The other major subject addressed at these annual meetings is the socio-political stability of the region, undermined by rising conflict and security fragility. An increase in WAEMU military spending has been observed and this weighs on state budgets, to the detriment of investment in socio-economic development. The Governor insisted on the need for a balanced approach in the allocation of public resources. "Strengthened security is essential to protect infrastructure and encourage foreign investment, but it must not compromise the financing of social and economic development," Jean-Claude Kassi Brou states.

The region must also meet the employment challenge for its largely young population. Jean-Claude Kassi Brou underlined the importance of strengthening human capital and creating job opportunities adapted to the needs of the market. "The employment challenge is urgent. We must explore strategies that promote the professional integration of young people, notably through entrepreneurship and digitalisation," he indicated, calling for greater engagement from international actors to support employment initiatives in emerging economies. The BCEAO Governor insisted on the need for coordinated action and strengthened international cooperation. He argued for the adaptation of global financial instruments to the specificities of developing countries. The annual meetings of the World Bank and the IMF offered the countries of the region a platform to defend their interests and promote a vision of inclusive and sustainable growth.

a5755.t:
The World Bank on Thursday said economic activity in Sub-Saharan Africa is projected to edge up from 3.3 per cent in 2024 to 3.5 per cent in 2025 and further accelerate to 4.3 per cent in 2026–27.
However, the bank said the region’s economic performance is still dragged down by some of its largest countries—namely, Angola, Nigeria, and South Africa.
“Excluding these countries, the rest of the subcontinent is expected to grow at 4.6 per cent in 2025 and speed up to 5.7 percent in 2026–27. This outlook is subject to heightened risks arising from global policy uncertainty,” the bank said in its latest Africa’s Pulse report released on the sidelines of the World Bank/IMF meetings in Washington.
“As inflation cools down and converges to targets, and (global and domestic) financial conditions remain accommodative, it is expected that household consumption and investment will support the region’s growth acceleration.”
The bank said the contribution of government consumption will remain modest as the public sector continues to balance revenues and expenditures while managing painful trade-offs between servicing the debt burden and investing in social and physical infrastructure.
Across sectors of economic activity, the contribution of services is expected to remain robust in 2025–27, primarily driven by recoveries in information and communications technology, the financial sector, and tourism, it added.
Agriculture is expected to pick up from its lows in 2023 and 2024, thanks to improved climate conditions, infrastructure, and technology. But despite the baseline forecasts of growth acceleration in the region during 2025–27, risks to the outlook remain tilted to the downside.
“Sub-Saharan African economies will navigate an uncertain landscape amid greater policy uncertainty, which may lead to changes in the world trade order; ongoing (regional and national) geopolitical shifts that may affect commodity prices, disrupt international relations, and yield further fragmentation; reduced foreign aid budgets worldwide; and challenges posed by extreme weather events.”
In per capita terms, growth in the region has been inadequate to yield significant reductions in extreme poverty, the report said.
Real income per capita in 2025 is expected to be around 2 per cent below its most recent peak in 2015. The per capita growth acceleration expected in 2025–27, at an annual average rate of 1.8 per cent, will contribute to a modest decline in the poverty rate.
The World Bank said forecasts indicate that after reaching a peak of 43.9 per cent in 2025, poverty, measured at $2.15 per capita per day in 2017 international purchasing power parity, will drop to 43.2 percent in 2027. Limited investments in income-generating sectors for the poor, lingering effects of past inflation, and the probable reduction of donor aid budgets worldwide pose a challenge for poverty reduction.
Inflation
The median inflation rate in Sub-Saharan Africa declined from 7.1 per cent in 2023 to 4.5 per cent in 2024, and it is projected to bounce back slightly to an annual average rate of 4.6 per cent in 2025–27, the report said.
A deceleration of inflation was recorded by about 70 per cent of the countries in the region in 2024 and the drop for most countries can be explained by the gradual easing of supply chain pressures, the effects of contractionary monetary and fiscal policy, as well as greater currency stability.
“However, the variability of inflation across countries remains high: of 47 countries in the region, 14 still have inflation rates of two digits or more—including Angola, Ethiopia, Ghana, Malawi, Nigeria, Sudan, and Zimbabwe, among others.
“By 2027, the number of countries with two-digit or higher inflation rates is expected to fall to six,” the report said.
